implementation_notes: JavaScript has no operator overloading, so the instance is an object with combine and identity fields, or a pair of functions passed to a generic fold. Array.prototype.reduce requires an initial value, and passing [] as the seed is the idiomatic identity for the concatenation monoid. Real cost trap: repeated string += is quadratic and engines no longer optimise it away reliably - use an array joined at the end, or a rope. Object spread and Object.assign are associative merges but lose key order determinism only in the sense that integer-like keys are reordered by the engine, which is observable.
idiom_name: instance object with identity and combine; Array.reduce with the identity seed
pitfalls: [].concat / spread is O(n) per call when it copies; accumulate parts in an array and join once.
Repeated s += t in a loop is quadratic in principle and cannot be relied on to be optimised; collect and join.
Array.prototype.reduce without an initial value throws on an empty array and silently uses the first element instead of the identity - always pass the seed explicitly.
Spread on a large object copies the whole shape each time; Object.assign into a preallocated target is the associative fold with less churn.
